explanation: Head-on elastic collision triggers many substeps (35-42 per step). Vertical velocity grows far faster than gravity*dt (vy=-6.39 after 0.133s vs expected -1.31), adding ~400J of spurious kinetic energy shared equally by both bodies. Likely gravity is over-integrated when substepping fast bodies, so energy_bound is violated even though the horizontal collision itself is reasonable.
vision_note: Two circles start almost touching near the top and then rapidly fly apart horizontally over steps 1 to 4. They stay high in the arena with little visible falling and no walls, controller or red highlight visible. [disagreement: The explanation blames spurious vertical velocity from over-integrated gravity shared equally, but the strip shows almost no vertical drop and instead a large, asymmetric horizontal separation, so the visible energy gain looks horizontal rather than vertical.]
